title: File the business tangible personal property (and machinery and tools) return
question: My business owns furniture, equipment or machinery in Staunton. What do I file, and by when?
office: Commissioner of the Revenue (assessment); City Treasurer (billing and collection)
summary: Every business in Staunton must report the furniture, fixtures, equipment, machinery and tools it owns or uses on January 1 to the Commissioner of the Revenue. Send an itemized list of all assets, including fully depreciated items, with the year acquired and original cost, by May 1. First-time filers use the city's 2026 Business Personal Property Form; businesses that filed before get last year's asset list in late March. File by mail, fax or email; no online filing route was found, and no filing fee is stated. The Commissioner values the property, and the Treasurer bills it. Payment is due December 5. Rates: $2.90 per $100 of assessed value for personal property, $1.24 for machinery and tools.

legal_basis.quote: Such tangible personal property is hereby segregated for and made subject to local taxation only pursuant to Article X, § 4 of the Constitution of Virginia.

Every taxpayer owning any of the property subject to taxation under this chapter on January 1 of any year shall file a return thereof with the commissioner of the revenue for his county or city on the appropriate forms
Such returns shall be filed on or before May 1 of each year, except as otherwise provided by ordinance authorized by § 58.1-3916

Every person who leases any of such property from the owner thereof on such date shall file a return with the commissioner of the revenue of the county or city wherein such property is located giving the name and address of the owner

Every taxpayer owning machinery and tools or business personal property, if requested by the commissioner of the revenue, shall include on his annual return of such property information as to the total of original cost by year of purchase.
The cost should be the original capitalized cost or the cost that would have been capitalized if the expense deduction in lieu of depreciation was elected under § 179 of the Internal Revenue Code.

steps.step: Check whether your business must file
steps.who: Business owner (any business with property in the city)
steps.how: If your business is in Staunton and owns or uses furniture, fixtures, equipment, machinery or tools on January 1, you must report them; the city's new business brochure says every business located in the city must file this return by May 1. Include items you have fully depreciated. If you lease equipment from its owner, state law also requires a return giving the owner's name and address (see caveats: the city's form has no section for this). The city's form and business pages do not say whether business vehicles go on this return (see caveats). Under state law the Commissioner may choose not to require a return for property too low in value to produce a tax, but the city's pages do not say it uses this option.
steps.deadline: Property owned or used on January 1 (the tax day)
steps.quote: The City of Staunton levies a tax on tangible personal property employed in a trade or business, including furniture, fixtures, equipment, machinery, tools, etc.

steps.step: Work out whether you report business personal property or machinery and tools
steps.who: Business owner; the Commissioner of the Revenue sets the classification
steps.how: Machinery and tools used in manufacturing, mining, water well drilling, processing or reprocessing, radio or television broadcasting, a dairy, dry cleaning or laundry business, or advanced recycling are taxed as machinery and tools, at $1.24 per $100 (idle machinery and tools are not; see s6). For these businesses, vehicles registered with the DMV are taxed as personal property, but other motor vehicles and delivery equipment are taxed as machinery and tools. Everything else used in a business, including computers, is business tangible personal property, at $2.90 per $100. State law caps the machinery and tools rate at the rate on the general class of tangible personal property. The city posts only one return form. If you think you have machinery and tools, ask the Commissioner's office how to report them (540.332.3829).
steps.quote: used in a manufacturing, mining, water well drilling, processing or reprocessing, radio or television broadcasting, dairy, dry cleaning or laundry business, or a business primarily engaged in advanced recycling

steps.step: Get the right return: the city's form for first-time filers, or the asset list the Commissioner mails to returning filers
steps.who: Commissioner of the Revenue (mails prior-year lists); business owner
steps.how: If your business has never filed in Staunton, use the 2026 Business Personal Property Form (titled Initial Return of Tangible Property) from the Business License & Taxes page. If you have filed before, the Commissioner mails you last year's asset list in late March. Update that list and return it. If it has not arrived, call the office.
steps.deadline: Prior-year lists are mailed in late March
steps.quote: If your business has filed a form before, a prior year asset list will be sent to you in late March.

steps.step: Prepare an itemized list of every asset, including fully depreciated items
steps.how: On the form, fill in the business details (trade name, contact name, address, phone, fax, email, SSN or FEIN). Then list each asset: quantity, year acquired, description, serial number if there is one, and original cost. Attach extra pages if you need them. Under state law the cost is the original capitalized cost, or what would have been capitalized if you took the section 179 expense deduction. Keep the records behind the list; the Commissioner can ask to check them.
steps.quote: A list of fixed assets itemizing all property (including all fully depreciated items) must be submitted.

steps.step: If you have no business equipment, still return the form and explain why
steps.how: Tick the box for no business equipment to file and write an explanation in the space provided.
steps.deadline: Same due date as the return (May 1)
steps.quote: IF YOU HAVE ZERO PROPERTY TO DECLARE, PLEASE CHECK THE BOX AND PROVIDE AN EXPLANATION.

steps.step: Manufacturers: report machinery and tools you will idle in writing by April 1
steps.who: Machinery and tools taxpayer, writing to the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Idle machinery and tools are not taxed as machinery and tools; state law makes them taxable as capital under § 58.1-1101 instead. Idle means out of use on the tax day, with no reasonable prospect of returning to use that year, and either out of use continuously for at least a year before the tax day, or identified to the Commissioner in writing by April 1 as equipment you intend to withdraw from service by the next tax day. If equipment you identified that way goes back into use, tell the Commissioner in writing by the next return due date, without extension. It is then taxed as if it had been in use on that year's tax day, with interest; with timely notice no penalty is charged. This comes from state law; the city's pages do not describe it.
steps.deadline: On or before April 1 (for withdrawal from service by the next January 1); notice of return to use by the next return due date, without extension
steps.quote: have been specifically identified in writing by the taxpayer to the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official, on or before April 1 of such year

steps.step: Sign and file the return with the Commissioner of the Revenue by May 1
steps.who: Business owner, filing with the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Sign and date the declaration at the bottom of the form. The form asks you to mail it to the Commissioner of the Revenue, P.O. Box 4, Staunton, VA 24402, fax it to 540.851.4022, or email it to revenue@ci.staunton.va.us. It does not mention hand delivery; the Commissioner's office is on the first floor of City Hall, 116 W. Beverley St., so ask the office if you want to drop it off. No online filing route was found. The form asks for no payment; the Treasurer bills the tax later. The form warns that willfully signing a return you do not believe to be true and correct is a misdemeanor; Va. Code § 58.1-11 makes it a Class 1 misdemeanor.
steps.quote: This annual business personal property tax return must be filed with the Commissioner of the Revenue by May 1st.

steps.step: If you do not file, the Commissioner assesses you anyway
steps.how: Without a return, the Commissioner enters a value from the best information available and assesses the tax as if you had reported it. The City Code also makes failing to file the personal property list on time a Class 4 misdemeanor, with a fine of up to $250 (City Code § 3.10.010; not quoted, see caveats). No civil late-filing penalty was found on the city's pages or in the City Code chapter read.
steps.quote: the commissioner of the revenue shall, from the best information he can obtain, enter the fair market value of such property and assess the same as if it had been reported to him.

steps.step: The Commissioner of the Revenue values the property
steps.how: The city publishes a business personal property trending schedule. It sets a 'Percent Good' by the item's age for 3, 5, 7, 10 and 15-year classes. For example, the 5-year class runs 95, 80, 60 and 40 percent, then 20 percent from the fifth year on. The 10-year class runs from 95 percent down to 10 percent. The schedule does not say which assets go in which class (see caveats). On request, the Commissioner must take the condition of the property into account, including technological obsolescence where that is an appropriate factor, and must make a reasonable description of the valuation methods available. For machinery and tools, the Commissioner must consider a bona fide, independent appraisal you present, on your written request. Under the City Code, a Commissioner who is not satisfied with your valuation may adopt a fair valuation, giving you a chance to be heard where practicable (City Code § 3.10.010, paraphrased).
steps.quote: The Commissioner of Revenue calculates the value of personal property, business personal property and machinery and tools and processes state income tax returns.

steps.step: The City Treasurer mails the tax bill
steps.how: The Treasurer bills and collects the tax. State law requires the bill to be mailed at least 14 days before the due date, and lets the Treasurer choose not to send a bill of $20 or less. The city's pages do not say when business bills go out.
steps.deadline: At least 14 days before the December 5 due date (state law)
steps.quote: not later than 14 days prior to the due date of the taxes, send or cause to be sent by United States mail to each taxpayer assessed with taxes and levies for that year a bill or bills setting forth the amounts due

steps.who: Business owner, paying the City Treasurer
steps.how: Pay in one of five ways. Online: the Treasurer's self-service site, which needs a web user account linked to your personal property account. By phone: call 1.888.272.9829, choose option 3, enter jurisdiction code 1038 and press 1 for personal property. In person: the Treasurer's Office, first floor of City Hall, 116 W. Beverley Street, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday. Drop box: the green box on Central Avenue under the clock tower, or the box inside City Hall in front of the Treasurer's office during business hours (check or money order). By mail: a check or money order payable to the City of Staunton, sent to the Treasurer at P.O. Box 474, Staunton, VA 24402-0474. Card and eCheck payments online or by phone carry a fee charged by the service provider. A returned check costs $20 under the City Code (§ 3.05.070, paraphrased). If December 5 falls on a day the office is closed, you can pay the next business day without penalty.
steps.deadline: December 5 (the next business day if the office is closed that day)
steps.fee: $2.90 per $100 of assessed value (personal property) or $1.24 per $100 (machinery and tools); provider fees of 2.35% for cards and $0.25 per eCheck
steps.quote: The payment date of business tangible personal property tax is December 5th.

steps.step: If you pay late: penalty, interest, collection fees, and no business licence
steps.who: City Treasurer; Commissioner of the Revenue (business licences)
steps.how: The City Code adds a 10 percent penalty to taxes not paid by the due date, and interest at 10 percent a year from January 1 of the following year (City Code § 3.10.040). It also charges collection fees: $30 on a delinquent account collected 30 or more days after a delinquency notice, $35 after judgment, and attorney or collection agency fees of up to 20 percent (City Code § 3.05.090). These City Code terms are paraphrased, not quoted (see caveats). The Commissioner will not issue a business licence while the business owes delinquent personal property tax.
steps.deadline: Penalty applies after December 5; interest from January 1 of the next year
steps.fee: 10% penalty; 10% a year interest; $30 or $35 administrative fee on delinquent accounts (City Code, paraphrased)
steps.quote: No business license will be issued until all delinquent business license and personal property taxes owed by the applicant to the City of Staunton have been paid (VA Code 58.1-3700).

steps.step: If you think the assessment is wrong, appeal to the Commissioner of the Revenue in writing
steps.who: Business owner, applying to the Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Write to the Commissioner in good faith. Identify the business, the tax year, the amount in dispute, each error you see, why it is wrong, and the relief you want. The assessment is presumed correct, so include your evidence. The Commissioner may hold a conference if you ask for one, or ask for more documents or an audit. The Commissioner must answer in writing within 90 days and explain your right to appeal to the Tax Commissioner. While a timely, complete appeal is pending, the Treasurer suspends collection unless collection would be jeopardized by delay or you have not answered a request for information; interest still accrues, but no further penalty. Paying the part you do not dispute is the cautious course. If you are denied, see the escalation section.
steps.deadline: Within one year from the last day of the tax year or one year from the assessment, whichever is later (Va. Code § 58.1-3983.1(B)(1)); the general correction statute allows three years from the end of the tax year (§ 58.1-3980(A))
steps.quote: The appeal shall be filed in good faith and sufficiently identify the taxpayer, the tax period covered by the challenged assessment, the amount in dispute, the remedy sought, each alleged error in the assessment, the grounds upon which the taxpayer relies, and any other facts relevant to the taxpayer's contention.

escalation.trigger: Assessment believed wrong, including one made because no return was filed
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue (administrative appeal, or written application for correction)
escalation.deadline: Within one year from the last day of the tax year or one year from the assessment, whichever is later (the general correction statute, § 58.1-3980(A), allows three years from the end of the tax year)
escalation.quote: may appeal such assessment within one year from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of such assessment, whichever is later, to the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: A timely and complete appeal is filed with the Commissioner
escalation.next: City Treasurer suspends collection until the Commissioner's final determination, unless collection would be jeopardized by delay or the taxpayer has not answered a request for information (interest still accrues; no further penalty)
escalation.quote: collection activity shall be suspended by the treasurer or other official responsible for the collection of such tax until a final determination is issued by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: No final determination from the Commissioner after the appeal has been pending more than one year
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (Virginia Department of Taxation), after at least 30 days' written notice to the Commissioner of the Revenue
escalation.deadline: After more than one year without a final determination, on at least 30 days' written notice
escalation.quote: elect to treat the application as denied and appeal the assessment to the Tax Commissioner in accordance with the provisions of subsection D

escalation.trigger: Commissioner denies the appeal in whole or in part
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (Virginia Department of Taxation), using the Appeals Form; serve a copy on the Commissioner of the Revenue. Include a copy of the Commissioner's written determination and a statement of the facts and grounds. A notice of intent to appeal further suspends collection, but the suspension ends unless the appeal is filed and served within 30 days of the notice (§ 58.1-3983.1(E)). The Tax Commissioner decides within 90 days of receiving the appeal, or up to 60 days later with notice (§ 58.1-3983.1(D)(3)).
escalation.deadline: Within 90 days of the date of the Commissioner's determination
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3983.1(D)(1), (D)(3) and (E); Virginia Tax, Administrative Appeals page
escalation.quote: may appeal the determination of the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official by filing an appeal with the Tax Commissioner and serving a copy of the appeal upon the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official within 90 days of the date of the determination of the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: Still aggrieved after the Tax Commissioner's final determination, or choosing to go straight to court
escalation.next: Circuit Court of the City of Staunton (the City of Staunton is the named party). The taxpayer must show the property was valued above fair market value, or the assessment is not uniform or is otherwise invalid or illegal. Going straight to court skips the collection suspension of § 58.1-3983.1(H).
escalation.deadline: Whichever is latest: three years from the last day of the tax year, one year from the assessment, one year from the Tax Commissioner's final determination, or one year from the Commissioner's final determination under § 58.1-3981
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made

escalation.trigger: Late payment penalty or interest charged when the lateness was not the taxpayer's fault
escalation.quote: The treasurer shall make determinations of fault relating exclusively to failure to pay a tax

escalation.trigger: Penalty for late filing charged when the late filing was not the taxpayer's fault
escalation.quote: the commissioner of the revenue shall make determinations of fault relating exclusively to failure to file a return

escalation.trigger: Unsure how the tax applies to a specific situation
escalation.quote: may request a written ruling regarding the application of a local mobile property tax or a local business tax to a specific situation from the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official

escalation.trigger: An assessment that can be appealed to the Tax Commissioner raises a question of interpretation
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (advisory opinion; Virginia Tax says such requests go on Form Rulings-Fee and may carry a fee)
escalation.quote: The Tax Commissioner shall have the authority to issue advisory written opinions in specific cases as requested to interpret a local business tax

escalation.trigger: Correction granted after the tax was paid
escalation.next: City Treasurer refunds the excess. State law requires the Commissioner's certificate, with the City Attorney's consent, and lets the governing body authorize the Treasurer to approve refunds up to $10,000. Under the City Code the refund includes any penalty and interest paid, plus interest at the city's delinquent-tax rate (City Code §§ 3.55.010, 3.55.020, paraphrased; no refund under that chapter if the application came more than three years after the end of the tax year).
escalation.quote: direct the treasurer of the county, city or town to refund the excess to the taxpayer

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

The city quotes and facts rest on Internet Archive copies: the Business License & Taxes page (captured 2026-08-09), the Taxes page (2026-08-22), Paying Taxes & Fees, the Commissioner of Revenue and Treasurer pages (2026-07-17), the Personal Property and Paying Personal Property Online pages (2026-04-13), Local Tax Forms (2026-02-15), the 2026 form (2026-06-07), and the business licence application, trending schedule and new business brochure (2025-09-17). A change to the live pages after those copies would not show here; anything on this page that those copies do not hold is marked as not confirmed.

Local code is cited, not quoted. Staunton's Code is published on eCode360 (General Code). Its Terms of Use forbid copying or republishing content for public purposes, so no City Code text is quoted. The penalty, interest, fee, misdemeanor and refund terms attributed to City Code §§ 3.10.010, 3.10.040, 3.05.070, 3.05.090, 3.55.010 and 3.55.020 are paraphrased. eCode360's terms say its copies should not be relied on as the definitive authority; on 2026-10-11 its New Laws list for Staunton showed three uncodified ordinances (2026-26, 2026-27 and 2026-28), none affecting Title 3. Confirm with the Commissioner, the Treasurer or the Clerk of Council before relying on them.

Filing date. The city states May 1, which matches the state default (Va. Code § 58.1-3518). City Code § 3.10.010 (paraphrased) defers to state law on who files, when and how. No local ordinance setting a different date was found.

The business personal property rate is inferred. The Taxes page lists one personal property rate ($2.90) and a separate machinery and tools rate ($1.24). It does not list a separate business rate. City Code § 3.10.010 (paraphrased) applies one rate to all taxable tangible personal property and leaves it to the annual budget ordinance. That ordinance for tax year 2026 was not read: the May 14 and May 28, 2026 City Council minutes have no text layer, and the adopted budget was not opened. The FY 2027 Budget in Brief also says both rates stay unchanged; its text uses embedded glyph codes, so it is not quoted. Rates are set yearly.

Valuation. The trending schedule PDF is named 'Trending Schedule 2022.pdf'. It shows percent-good tables only. It does not say which assets fall in the 3, 5, 7, 10 or 15-year classes, or whether the percentage is applied to original cost (state law, § 58.1-3503(A)(18), requires a percentage of original cost). No method for valuing machinery and tools is published. Ask the Commissioner for its written description of valuation methods (§ 58.1-3503(B)).
Machinery and tools. The city posts no separate machinery and tools return. Whether manufacturers use the same form or get a different one from the Commissioner was not found.

Leased equipment. State law requires a business that leases equipment from its owner to file a return giving the owner's name and address (§ 58.1-3518). The city's 2026 form has no section for leased property, and the city's pages do not mention it. Ask the Commissioner how to report it.

Business vehicles. Neither the city's 2026 form nor its business pages or brochure say whether business vehicles go on this return. City Code § 3.10.010 (paraphrased) has motor vehicle owners file a new return by May 1 when a vehicle is bought or sold or its details change, and otherwise assesses vehicles from the last return or DMV records. For manufacturers and the other machinery and tools businesses, vehicles not registered with the DMV and delivery equipment are machinery and tools (§ 58.1-3507(C)). Ask the Commissioner how to report business vehicles.

Late filing. No civil late-filing penalty was found on the city's pages or in City Code chapter 3.10. That chapter makes failure to file on time a Class 4 misdemeanor (paraphrased). State law would allow a penalty of up to 10% of the tax or $10 (§ 58.1-3916). Whether City Council has authorized filing extensions (up to 90 days by resolution, § 58.1-3916) was not found.

Penalty rate. City Code § 3.10.040 (paraphrased) sets a 10% late-payment penalty. State law would allow 25% on tangible personal property more than 30 days past due, but no Staunton provision for that was found.

Closing, selling or moving the business. The city's pages say nothing about proration of business property. State law fixes status and value on January 1 (§ 58.1-3515), and its proration option (§ 58.1-3516) covers motor vehicles, trailers, semitrailers and boats only. Expect a full year's tax, and confirm with the Commissioner. How to report a closure was not found for business personal property. The brochure says a business licence is closed by written notice.

Billing. The city's pages do not say when business personal property bills are mailed. State law requires mailing at least 14 days before the due date (§ 58.1-3912(A)). Whether business bills can be paid on the Treasurer's self-service site is not stated separately; the site requires a web user account and was not opened.

The 2026 form's year. The Internet Archive copy of the form reads 'DUE MAY 1, 2026' (the last digit of the year is drawn with an embedded glyph). The page's link text ('2026 Business Personal Property Form') and the file name ('BT Return Blank May 1 2026.pdf') agree. The form has no fillable fields.
False return. The form warns that willfully subscribing a false return is a misdemeanor and cites Va. Code § 58.1-11, which makes it a Class 1 misdemeanor.

Appeals and payment. Collection is suspended while a timely, complete appeal is pending (§ 58.1-3983.1(C)), and a bill is not delinquent while an appeal filed within 90 days of the assessment is pending (§ 58.1-3916; City Code § 3.05.090, paraphrased). Interest still accrues. Paying the undisputed amount on time is the cautious course.

The Tax Commissioner's Appeals Form and Form Rulings-Fee were not opened. Their URLs come from Virginia Tax's Administrative Appeals page, which says the taxpayer must give the local assessing officer a copy of any appeal filed with the Tax Commissioner.

Privacy. City pages and forms name the Commissioner and the Treasurer and link their personal mailboxes; the court page names the clerk and judges. All of these were left out. Only office lines, office addresses and the role mailbox revenue@ci.staunton.va.us, printed on the Commissioner's own forms, are recorded. No circuit court clerk's mailbox is recorded.

corrections: Quotes: all 67 draft quotes were confirmed word for word. The 53 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised), and their subsection labels match the text. The 14 city quotes were matched against Internet Archive copies of the cited www.ci.staunton.va.us pages and PDFs, fetched read-only with the research User-Agent (the live site still answers HTTP 403, robots.txt included): Business License & Taxes (captured 2026-08-09), Taxes (2026-08-22), Paying Taxes & Fees (2026-07-17), the 2026 form (2026-06-07), the business licence application and the trending schedule (2025-09-17). 11 state-law quotes were added and checked the same way (§§ 58.1-3507(A), (C) and (E), 58.1-3912(A), 15.2-106, 58.1-3983.1(B)(4), (D)(1) and (E), 58.1-3981(A), 58.1-3984(A)). The 6 short quotes in prose (file names, link text, 'DUE MAY 1, 2026', 'Percent Good') were also confirmed.

City Code paraphrases (§§ 3.10.010(1), (4), (5); 3.10.040(2), (4); 3.05.090(1), (2), (4); 3.55.010(1), (5); 3.55.020) were read on eCode360 with the research User-Agent (robots.txt allows section pages) and match what the file says. eCode360's New Laws list shows no uncodified ordinance affecting Title 3.
Summary: 'there is no filing fee' overstated the sources, which state no fee; now 'no filing fee is stated'.

s1: 'Leave out vehicles; they are handled as ordinary personal property' had no source (the form, Business License & Taxes page and brochure say nothing about vehicles); removed and replaced with a pointer to a new caveat. 'Lease, rent or borrow' went beyond § 58.1-3518, which covers a person who leases property from its owner; reworded. Added the brochure's statement that every business located in the city must file by May 1.

s2: added that idle machinery and tools are excluded, that for machinery and tools businesses DMV-registered vehicles are personal property but other vehicles and delivery equipment are machinery and tools (§ 58.1-3507(C)), and the state cap on the machinery and tools rate (§ 58.1-3507(A)).

s6: the return-to-use notice applies only to equipment idled under the April 1 identification route (§ 58.1-3507(E)); added that it must be given without extension, that the tax then applies as if in use on that tax day with interest, and that timely notice avoids a penalty. Deadline reworded from 'April 1 of the tax year' to the statute's terms (by April 1, for withdrawal by the next tax day).

s7: 'You can also bring it to the office' had no source; the form lists only mail, fax and email. Reworded to say hand delivery is not mentioned and to ask the office. 'Do not send payment' is now 'the form asks for no payment'. 'A knowingly false return is a crime' now follows § 58.1-11 and the form: willfully signing a return you do not believe to be true and correct is a Class 1 misdemeanor.

s9: technological obsolescence counts where it is an appropriate factor, the Commissioner must make a reasonable description of valuation methods available on request, and the machinery and tools appraisal must be bona fide and independent, on written request (§§ 58.1-3503(B), 58.1-3507(B)). Added City Code § 3.10.010(3) (paraphrased): the Commissioner may adopt a fair valuation, with a chance to be heard where practicable.
s10: added that the Treasurer may elect not to send a bill of $20 or less (§ 58.1-3912(A)).
s11: added the drop box inside City Hall in front of the Treasurer's office during business hours (Taxes page) and the $20 returned-check fee (City Code § 3.05.070, paraphrased).

s13: added that the assessment is deemed prima facie correct (§ 58.1-3983.1(B)(4)) and the two exceptions to the suspension of collection (jeopardy; no answer to a request for information) (§ 58.1-3983.1(C)).
Fees: added the returned-check fee ($20, City Code § 3.05.070; cap $50, § 15.2-106).
Escalation rung 2: added the two exceptions to the suspension of collection (§ 58.1-3983.1(C)).

Escalation rung 4: added the required contents of the appeal (§ 58.1-3983.1(D)(1)), the notice-of-intent suspension and its 30-day limit (§ 58.1-3983.1(E)), and the Tax Commissioner's 90-day determination with up to 60 more days (§ 58.1-3983.1(D)(3)).
Escalation rung 5: added the taxpayer's burden in circuit court (§ 58.1-3984(A)).

Escalation rung 10: added the state refund conditions (Commissioner's certificate with the City Attorney's consent; Treasurer may be authorized to approve refunds up to $10,000, § 58.1-3981(A)) and the City Code interest on refunds (§ 3.55.020, paraphrased).
Legal basis: added the 10 state entries above and local entries for City Code §§ 3.55.020 and 3.05.070 (cited, not quoted).

Caveats: added a verification-access caveat and a business-vehicles caveat; fixed the leased-equipment caveat (leases, not rents or borrows); the 2026 form's year reads 'DUE MAY 1, 2026' in the verifier's pdftotext extraction; the eCode360 currency note now cites its terms and New Laws list.
Sources: the business licence application title no longer says 'updated August 2024', which the PDF text does not show; added § 15.2-106.

Checked and unchanged: contacts (Commissioner and Treasurer pages, the form, Paying Taxes & Fees, Virginia Tax's Administrative Appeals page, the Staunton Circuit Court page) are office channels only; staff names and personal mailboxes on those pages are not recorded. Rates ($2.90 and $1.24), the May 1 and December 5 dates, the next-business-day rule, the phone payment steps and provider fees match the city pages.
